CHART CODE:
 import plotly.express as px

data = {
    "Age Group": ["4-6", "4-6", "4-6", "7-9", "7-9", "7-9", "10-12", "10-12", "10-12"],
    "Admission Stage": ["Applicant", "Approved", "Enrolled", "Applicant", "Approved", "Enrolled", "Applicant", "Approved", "Enrolled"],
    "Count": [250, 240, 235, 145, 138, 130, 50, 42, 35],
    "Retention Rate (%)": [92, 95, 97, 88, 91, 94, 78, 82, 86],
    "Processing Time (days)": [12, 8, 5, 15, 10, 7, 18, 12, 9]
}

fig = px.scatter(
    data,
    x="Retention Rate (%)",
    y="Processing Time (days)",
    size="Count",
    color="Age Group",
    hover_name="Admission Stage",
    size_max=60,
    color_discrete_sequence=["#FF6B6B", "#4ECDC4", "#45B7D1"],
    title="Primary School Admissions: Retention vs Processing Time by Age Group (Barbados 2023)"
)

fig.update_layout(
    xaxis_title="Retention Rate (%)",
    yaxis_title="Processing Time (days)",
    legend_title="Age Group",
    font=dict(size=12),
    margin=dict(l=50, r=50, t=80, b=50),
    hoverlabel=dict(font_size=12)
)

fig.update_traces(
    marker=dict(line=dict(width=1, color='DarkSlateGrey')),
    selector=dict(mode='markers')
)

fig.write_image("output.png")

SUMMARY:
 The chart presented is a bubble chart titled "Primary School Admissions: Retention vs Processing Time by Age Group (Barbados 2023)." It illustrates the relationship between retention rate and processing time for primary school admissions across three distinct age groups. The horizontal axis represents the retention rate in percentage, ranging from 75% to 100%, while the vertical axis shows the processing time in days, spanning from 1 to 20 days.

Three age groups are color-coded for easy differentiation: the 4-6 age group is represented in a light teal shade, the 7-9 age group in a soft yellow, and the 10-12 age group in a pale peach color. Each bubble corresponds to a specific admission stage, with its size indicating the count of admissions, though the exact counts are not visually labeled on the chart itself.

For the 4-6 age group, the bubbles show retention rates between approximately 92% and 97%, with processing times decreasing from 12 days to 5 days as retention improves. The 7-9 age group exhibits retention rates from about 88% to 94%, with processing times reducing from 15 days to 7 days. The 10-12 age group, which has the lowest retention rates ranging from 78% to 86%, displays processing times from 18 days down to 9 days. The largest bubbles, representing higher counts, generally appear in the younger age groups, particularly for the 4-6 and 7-9 categories. The bubbles are outlined with a thin dark gray border, enhancing their visibility against the chart’s light background.

p = Path("chart.py")
source = p.read_text()
source = source.replace(
    'color_discrete_sequence=["#FF6B6B", "#4ECDC4", "#45B7D1"]',
    'color_discrete_sequence=["#8DD3C7", "#FFFFB3", "#FDB462"]'
)
source = source.replace(
    '    xaxis_title="Retention Rate (%)",',
    '    xaxis_title="Retention Rate (%)",\n    xaxis_range=[75, 100],'
)
source = source.replace(
    '    yaxis_title="Processing Time (days)",',
    '    yaxis_title="Processing Time (days)",\n    yaxis_range=[1, 20],'
)
p.write_text(source)
exec(compile(source, "chart.py", "exec"))
import pandas as pd
table = pd.read_csv("table.csv")
for trace in fig.data:
    rows = table[table["Age Group"] == trace.name]
    assert list(trace.x) == rows["Retention Rate (%)"].tolist()
    assert list(trace.y) == rows["Processing Time (days)"].tolist()
    assert list(trace.marker.size) == rows["Count"].tolist()
    print(trace.name, trace.marker.color, list(trace.x), list(trace.y), list(trace.marker.size))
print("Axis ranges:", fig.layout.xaxis.range, fig.layout.yaxis.range)
print("Title:", fig.layout.title.text)
